mainTopic: The end of the יום הנף discussion, and the new משנה on the first day of סוכות falling on שבת: the need to own your לולב, the gift rule, and love of מצוות.
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a discussion about new grain (חדש). רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade eating it all of יום הנף, and the גמרא explains that this follows רבי יהודה's Torah-level reading of 'עד עצם היום הזה.' A ברייתא seems to show רבי יהודה arguing with him. The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה misunderstood him, and that 'הִתְקִין' means he expounded the פסוק and made it public practice. Then a new משנה begins. When the first day of סוכות falls on שבת, everyone brings his לולב to the בית הכנסת beforehand, because on the first day a person must use his own לולב. רבי יוסי adds that someone who forgot it was שבת and carried his לולב out is פטור. The גמרא learns the ownership rule from 'וּלְקַחְתֶּם' and 'לָכֶם', and shows it in action with four חכמים on a ship passing one לולב to each other as a gift. From that story it learns that a gift given on condition of return is a real gift, and רבא adds that the gift counts only if the item is actually returned. The גמרא then praises love of מצוות: אמימר prayed holding his לולב, a מצוה object does not distract a person during תפילה, and the people of ירושלים carried their לולב almost everywhere. At the end the גמרא returns to רבי יוסי's ruling, and אביי's comment on it continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The verse forbids new grain for the whole day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי יהודה's source. 'עד עצם היום הזה' means until the full body of the day, and 'עד' includes the day itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'until this very day,' which means until the very essence of the day. He also holds that 'until' includes the day itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer from the previous lines. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי follows רבי יהודה, and here is how רבי יהודה reads the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עצם is read as 'the full body' of the day, meaning the entire sixteenth of ניסן. Since 'עד' is inclusive (עד ועד בכלל), the ban on חדש lasts through the whole day. That is true whenever there is no עומר being brought.

keyTerms.meaning: The very day itself; the full body of the day
The essence or full extent of the day

steps.confusionAlert: 'עד ועד בכלל' does not mean the grain is allowed once the day begins. It means the day itself is included in the ban, so you may eat only after the whole day is over.

phrases.english: "Until this very day"
phrases.notes: ויקרא כ״ג:י״ד, about the ban on new grain

phrases.english: means until the essence (full body) of the day,
and he holds that "until" means until and including.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה — עַד עִיצּוּמוֹ שֶׁל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer on the previous עמוד, which said that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי follows רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מן התורה, new grain is forbidden through the entire day of יום הנף when no עומר is brought, because 'עד' is inclusive.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה arguing with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבן יוחנן בן זכאי can follow רבי יהודה. In a ברייתא, רבי יהודה protests against רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really agree with him? Doesn't he argue with him? A ברייתא teaches: after the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי enacted that the whole יום הנף is forbidden. רבי יהודה said to him: 'But it is already forbidden מן התורה! The פסוק says "until this very day," meaning until the essence of the day!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and רבי יהודה hold the same view. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה seems to disagree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי 'enacted' (הִתְקִין) the rule, which sounds like a rabbinic decree. רבי יהודה objects that it is already Torah law. If they argue, then רבן יוחנן בן זכאי cannot be following רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The day the עומר was waved (16 ניסן)

phrases.english: And does he really hold like him?
But he clearly argues with him,
as it is taught: once the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai enacted
that the entire day of waving should be forbidden.
Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
But isn't it forbidden by Torah law,
as it is written: "Until this very day"
— until the essence of the day!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ? וְהָא מִפְלָיג פְּלִיג עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי follows רבי יהודה's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה objects to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. People who argue with each other cannot hold the same view.

steps.title: רבי יהודה misunderstood רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: The argument in the ברייתא is not real. רבי יהודה thought the rule was rabbinic, but רבן יוחנן בן זכאי actually meant it as Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה who made the mistake. He thought רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was speaking of a rabbinic law. That is not so. He was speaking of a Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the 'argument' was only a misunderstanding on רבי יהודה's part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of them really agree that the ban comes מדאורייתא. רבי יהודה's protest was aimed at a position רבן יוחנן בן זכאי never held. So the two can still share the same view.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda who is mistaken;
he thought he was saying it by rabbinic law.
But that is not so; he was saying it by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the dispute as a misunderstanding
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי truly disagree about whether the ban is Torah law or rabbinic.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree that it is Torah law. רבי יהודה simply misread רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's intent.

steps.title: But the word 'הִתְקִין' sounds rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא says 'הִתְקִין' (enacted), which normally describes a rabbinic decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it says 'he enacted'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The wording of the ברייתא seems to support רבי יהודה's understanding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was only stating Torah law, why would the ברייתא say he 'enacted' it? An enactment (תקנה) usually means a new rabbinic rule.

phrases.english: But it says "he enacted"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3 from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant a Torah-level ban.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word הִתְקִין implies a rabbinic enactment, not a statement of Torah law.

steps.title: 'הִתְקִין' means he expounded and then set the practice
steps.stepSummary: 'הִתְקִין' here means that he expounded the פסוק and then established public practice based on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he enacted' mean? He expounded the פסוק, and then he established it as practice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reinterprets the word הִתְקִין. This ends the discussion of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי did not create a new rabbinic law. He taught the Torah meaning of the פסוק and made sure the public acted on it. That fits his following רבי יהודה's Torah-level reading.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this סוגיא, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's rule that new grain is forbidden all of יום הנף is Torah law, based on רבי יהודה's reading of 'עד עצם היום הזה.' The word 'הִתְקִין' only means he taught the פסוק and made it public practice.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "he enacted"?
He expounded the verse, and then established it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 and closes the sugya.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הִתְקִין means a new rabbinic decree.
steps.terutzMaskana: הִתְקִין means he taught the Torah law from the פסוק and set it as public practice.

steps.title: When the first day falls on שבת, everyone brings their לולב to shul beforehand
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. If the first day of סוכות is on שבת, people bring their לולבים to shul before שבת. In the morning, each person finds and takes his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the first day of the festival falls on שבת, all the people bring their לולבים to the shul. The next day they rise early and come, and each person recognizes his own לולב and takes it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a practical case: how to take the לולב on שבת without carrying it through the street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying in a רשות הרבים is forbidden on שבת. So the לולבים are brought to shul on ערב שבת, and on שבת everyone takes them right there. The משנה stresses that each person takes his own, and the next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the festival
That happens to fall on שבת

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The first day of the festival (Sukkot)
that falls on Shabbat:
all the people bring their lulavim
to the synagogue (before Shabbat).
The next day they rise early and come,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מַכִּיר אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ
phrases.english: each and every one recognizes his own
and takes it,

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, unrelated to the יום הנף discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a first day of סוכות that falls on שבת, the לולבים are brought to shul in advance, and each person takes his own.

steps.title: On the first day you must use your own לולב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains why each person takes his own לולב. On the first day you cannot be יוצא with someone else's לולב, but on the other days you can.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is because the חכמים said: a person does not fulfill his obligation on the first day with his friend's לולב. On the rest of the days of the festival, a person does fulfill his obligation with his friend's לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reason for the previous line. It is explaining why everyone must find his own לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day there is a requirement that the לולב belong to you. Using a borrowed one does not count. On the other days this requirement does not apply, so a borrowed לולב is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: The rest of the days of the festival

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known practice that on the first day of סוכות one must own the ארבעה מינים. A borrowed set does not work, which is why sets are given as a gift on condition that they be returned.

phrases.english: because the Sages said:
a person does not fulfill his obligation
on the first day of the festival
with the lulav of his friend;
and on the rest of the days of the festival,
a person does fulfill his obligation
with the lulav of his friend.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the practice described in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first day one must use his own לולב. On the other days a borrowed לולב is valid.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: carrying the לולב by mistake on שבת is פטור
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules on someone who forgot it was שבת on the first day of סוכות and carried his לולב into a רשות הרבים. He is פטור, because he carried it while busy with a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: if the first day of the festival fell on שבת, and a person forgot and carried the לולב out into the public domain, he is exempt, because he carried it out with permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with רבי יוסי's ruling on someone who accidentally broke שבת while doing the מצוה of לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an accidental act of carrying on שבת requires a קרבן חטאת. רבי יוסי says this person is exempt from that קרבן. Since he was busy with a מצוה, his act counts as done 'ברשות,' with permission.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt (here, from bringing a קרבן חטאת)

steps.confusionAlert: 'פטור' here does not mean carrying the לולב on שבת is allowed. It means only that this person, who did it by mistake while doing a מצוה, does not have to bring a קרבן חטאת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
If the first day of the festival
falls on Shabbat,
and he forgot and carried the lulav out
into the public domain,
he is exempt,
because he carried it out with permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further ruling to the same case of the first day falling on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who forgot and carried his לולב into a רשות הרבים on שבת while busy with the מצוה is exempt from a קרבן חטאת.

steps.title: Where do we learn that you need your own לולב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that on the first day you cannot be יוצא with someone else's לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking for the source of the rule. This question sets up the next step, where a ברייתא gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that on the first day of סוכות each person must use his own לולב, but it did not say why. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק this comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: 'These matters' refers to the משנה's rule that you cannot be יוצא with a friend's לולב on the first day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in the משנה (Step 7).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that on the first day of סוכות a person must use his own לולב.

steps.title: Learning the rule from 'וּלְקַחְתֶּם' and 'לָכֶם'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'וּלְקַחְתֶּם' that every person must take a לולב himself, and from 'לָכֶם' that it must be his own, not borrowed or stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'And you shall take' means that each and every person must do the taking. 'For yourselves' means from what is yours, which leaves out a borrowed or stolen לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא that reads two words of the פסוק closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וּלְקַחְתֶּם' is plural, so each person must take a לולב with his own hand, and one person cannot take it for everyone. 'לָכֶם' means 'yours', so a לולב that you borrowed (שאול) or stole (גזול) does not count, because it does not belong to you.

keyTerms.meaning: For yourselves, meaning from your own property

steps.confusionAlert: Borrowed and stolen are left out for the same reason. Neither one belongs to the person holding it, even though borrowing is permitted and stealing is not.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
'And you shall take' — that there should be a taking
phrases.notes: The verb is in the plural.

phrases.english: in the hand of each and every one.
'For yourselves' — from what is yours,
to exclude the borrowed and the stolen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'וּלְקַחְתֶּם' and 'לָכֶם' in the פסוק teach that each person must take a לולב that he owns.

steps.title: The practical rule: a friend's לולב works only as a gift
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים conclude that on the first day you are not יוצא with a friend's לולב unless he gives it to you as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here the חכמים said: a person is not יוצא on the first day of the festival with his friend's לולב, unless the friend gave it to him as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא turns the reading of the פסוק into a practical rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because 'לָכֶם' requires ownership, the way to use a friend's לולב is for the friend to give it to you as a real gift. Once you receive it as a gift, it belongs to you. The rule applies only to the first day, as the משנה said.

keyTerms.meaning: From here the Sages said (a rule drawn from the source)
A gift, which makes the receiver the full owner

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the common practice of giving a לולב and אתרוג to someone as a gift on the first day, so that he can be יוצא with them.

phrases.english: From here the Sages said:
A person does not fulfill his obligation
on the first day of the festival
with the lulav of his friend

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נְתָנוֹ לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה.
phrases.english: unless he gave it to him as a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical rule from the reading in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first day, a friend's לולב works only if he gives it to you as a real gift.

steps.title: The story begins: four חכמים on a ship with one לולב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells of four great חכמים traveling on a ship, where only רבן גמליאל had a לולב, which he had bought for a thousand זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story with רבן גמליאל, רבי יהושע, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא, who were traveling on a ship. Only רבן גמליאל had a לולב, and he had bought it for a thousand זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets up a story that shows the gift rule in action. This step gives the background, and the next step tells what they did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is that four people needed to be יוצא and there was only one לולב, which belonged to רבן גמליאל. The high price of a thousand זוז shows how precious the לולב was to them.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident used to show a הלכה in practice
A thousand זוז, a very large sum

phrases.english: And there was an incident with Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya and Rabbi Akiva
who were traveling on a ship,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה לוּלָב אֶלָּא לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּלְבַד,
phrases.english: and no one had a lulav except Rabban Gamliel alone,
which he had bought for a thousand zuz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a story that shows the rule of Step 11 being practiced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Background of the story: four people needed to be יוצא and only one of them owned a לולב.

steps.title: Passing the לולב from one חכם to the next as a gift
steps.stepSummary: Each חכם used the לולב and then gave it to the next as a gift. רבי עקיבא, the last one, returned it to רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל took it, was יוצא with it, and gave it to רבי יהושע as a gift. רבי יהושע took it, was יוצא, and gave it to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה as a gift. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה took it, was יוצא, and gave it as a gift to רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא took it, was יוצא, and returned it to רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows the rule of Step 11 in practice. Each person became the owner through a gift, so each one was יוצא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בְּמַתָּנָה' appears at every handoff, because owning the לולב was what made it work for each person. At the very end, רבי עקיבא gives it back, and the גמרא will ask about that detail next.

keyTerms.meaning: He fulfilled his obligation with it

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel took it and fulfilled his obligation with it,
and gave it to Rabbi Yehoshua as a gift.
Rabbi Yehoshua took it and fulfilled his obligation with it,

phrases.aramaic: וּנְתָנוֹ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה בְּמַתָּנָה.
phrases.english: and gave it to Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya as a gift.

phrases.aramaic: נְטָלוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְיָצָא בּוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya took it and fulfilled his obligation with it,
and gave it as a gift to Rabbi Akiva.
Rabbi Akiva took it and fulfilled his obligation with it,
and returned it to Rabban Gamliel.
phrases.notes: The גמרא will ask about this detail in the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Passing the לולב from person to person as a gift lets each person be יוצא on the first day.

steps.title: Why mention that רבי עקיבא returned it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to tell us that רבי עקיבא returned the לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need to be told that he returned it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices an extra detail at the end of the story and asks what it is there to teach. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main point of the story is that each חכם was יוצא through a gift. Returning the לולב at the end does not seem to add anything to that point, so the גמרא assumes it must be teaching something.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it to say? (asks about a detail that seems unnecessary)

phrases.english: Why do I need to say 'he returned it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the last detail of the story in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the detail 'וְהֶחְזִירוֹ' adds to the story.

steps.title: A gift given on condition it be returned is a real gift
steps.stepSummary: The detail teaches a side lesson: a gift given on condition that it be returned still counts as a real gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us something along the way: a gift given on condition that it be returned is called a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the detail about returning the לולב teaches a separate lesson along the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא was clearly expected to give the לולב back, yet he was still יוצא. So a gift does not stop being a gift just because it must be returned. For the time it is in your hands, it is fully yours, and that is enough for 'לָכֶם'.

keyTerms.meaning: A point taught in passing, as a side lesson
A gift given on condition that it be returned

steps.whatToRemember: מתנה על מנת להחזיר שמה מתנה: a gift given on condition that it be returned counts as a real gift, so the person who receives it can be יוצא with it on the first day.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a loan. A loan is never yours. A gift on condition of return is truly yours until you give it back, which is why it works for 'לָכֶם' when a borrowed לולב does not.

phrases.aramaic: מִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן:
phrases.english: It teaches us a matter in passing:

phrases.aramaic: מַתָּנָה עַל מְנָת לְהַחְזִיר — שְׁמָהּ מַתָּנָה.
phrases.english: a gift on condition to return it is called a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The return teaches that a gift given on condition of return is still a valid gift.

steps.title: רבא: an אתרוג given on condition of return, and what happens if it is not returned
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if someone receives an אתרוג on condition he return it, he is יוצא only if he actually returns it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: if someone says, 'Here is this אתרוג, on condition that you return it to me,' and the other person takes it and is יוצא with it, then if he returns it, he was יוצא. If he does not return it, he was not יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's ruling, which supports the same idea and adds a detail about what happens when the condition is broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees that such a gift works, but the condition matters. If the receiver returns the אתרוג, the gift was valid and he was יוצא. If he does not return it, the condition was broken, so the gift never took effect, and he was using an אתרוג that was never his.

keyTerms.meaning: Like that which he said (introduces a parallel source)

steps.whatToRemember: A gift on condition of return works only if the condition is kept. If the אתרוג is not returned, the gift is cancelled from the start, and the person was not יוצא.
steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, when giving a לולב and אתרוג on the first day 'on condition that you return it', the receiver must actually give it back. Otherwise his מצוה does not count.

phrases.english: Like that which Rava said:
'Here is this etrog for you'
'on condition that you return it to me.'
He took it and fulfilled his obligation with it:
if he returned it, he fulfilled his obligation;
if he did not return it, he did not fulfill his obligation.
phrases.notes: The condition was not kept, so the gift never took effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the principle of Step 15 with רבא's ruling and adds what happens when the condition is broken.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that a gift given on condition of return is a valid gift.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling about an אתרוג given 'on condition that you return it to me'.

steps.title: Why mention the thousand-זוז price?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to say that רבן גמליאל paid a thousand זוז for the לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need to be told that he bought it for a thousand זוז?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about another extra detail in the ship story. Why does the ברייתא bother to mention the price?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 14-15, the גמרא asked why the ברייתא mentions that רבי עקיבא returned the לולב. Now it asks the same kind of question about the price. The assumption is that every detail in a ברייתא should teach us something.

phrases.english: Why do I need to say
that he bought it for a thousand zuz?
phrases.notes: Refers to רבן גמליאל's לולב on the ship (step 12).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same kind of question as step 14, now aimed at a different detail of the ship story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the price detail in the ברייתא teaches.

steps.title: To show how beloved מצוות were to them
steps.stepSummary: The price is mentioned to show how much the חכמים loved מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: To let you know how beloved the מצוות were to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the price detail is there to teach us something. It shows how precious מצוות were to the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This detail does not teach a הלכה. It teaches an attitude. Paying a huge price for one לולב shows love of מצוות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This theme of love for the מצוה leads into the next topic, holding the לולב even during תפילה.

phrases.english: To inform you how much מצוות
were beloved to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The price shows how precious מצוות were to the חכמים.

steps.title: אמימר prayed holding the לולב
steps.stepSummary: מר בר אמימר tells רב אשי that his father, אמימר, prayed while holding the ארבעה מינים.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר אמימר said to רב אשי: My father would pray while holding it (the לולב).
steps.whatsHappening: A new report begins: אמימר used to hold his לולב during תפילה. This sets up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of love for the מצוה. אמימר did not put the לולב down even while praying. The question will be whether holding something during תפילה is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar bar Ameimar said to Rav Ashi:
My father would pray with it (in his hand).
phrases.notes: "It" means the לולב together with the other species.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic that connects to the theme of loving the מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may pray while holding the לולב, as אמימר did.

steps.title: Challenge: one may not pray holding objects
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids praying while holding תפילין or a ספר תורה, and שמואל adds ordinary objects like a knife or money. So how could אמימר pray holding a לולב?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: A person should not hold תפילין in his hand or a ספר תורה in his lap and pray. He should not urinate while holding them, and he should not sleep while holding them, whether a real sleep or a nap. And שמואל said: a knife, a bowl, a loaf of bread, or money are the same as those.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אמימר's practice. Sources say a person should not hold things while praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even holy objects like תפילין and a ספר תורה may not be held during תפילה. שמואל adds everyday items too, because the person worries they might fall and cannot focus on his תפילה. If so, a לולב should also be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Are like them, follow the same rule

steps.confusionAlert: The rules about urinating and sleeping are part of the quoted ברייתא. The challenge here only uses the part about praying.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A person should not hold tefillin in his hand
or a Torah scroll in his lap, and pray.
And he should not urinate holding them,
and he should not sleep holding them,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שֵׁינַת קֶבַע וְלֹא שֵׁינַת עֲרַאי.
phrases.english: neither a set sleep nor a brief nap.
And Shmuel said:
A knife and a bowl, a loaf and money —
these are like them (one may not pray holding them).
phrases.notes: He is busy worrying they will fall, so he cannot concentrate.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: לֹא יֹאחַז אָדָם תְּפִילִּין בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אמימר's practice from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's practice of praying while holding the לולב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holding any object during תפילה is forbidden because it distracts the person. A לולב should be no different.

steps.title: A מצוה object does not distract
steps.stepSummary: The other items are not מצוות, so they distract him. The לולב is a מצוה, so it does not distract him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, they are not מצוות, and he is distracted by them. Here, they are a מצוה, and he is not distracted by them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains why a לולב is different from a knife or money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the ban is distraction. A מצוה object held for the sake of the מצוה does not pull a person's mind away from תפילה, so the reason for the ban does not apply.
steps.confusionAlert: תפילין and a ספר תורה are holy too, yet they were forbidden. The answer is aimed at the case being compared here: at that moment, the לולב is being held as part of its own מצוה.

phrases.english: There, they are not a מצוה,
and he is distracted by them.
Here, they are a מצוה,
and he is not distracted by them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by pointing out a difference between the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any object held during תפילה distracts the person, including a לולב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only non-מצוה items distract. A מצוה item like the לולב does not, so holding it during תפילה is allowed.

steps.title: The people of ירושלים carried their לולב everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק describes how the people of ירושלים kept their לולב in hand all day, even during קריאת שמע and תפילה. They put it down only for certain activities.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק says, this was the custom of the people of ירושלים. A person left his house with his לולב in his hand. He went to the בית הכנסת with his לולב in his hand. He said קריאת שמע and prayed with his לולב in his hand. When he read the תורה or lifted his hands for ברכת כהנים, he put it on the ground. He went to visit the sick and comfort mourners with his לולב in his hand. When he entered the בית המדרש, he sent his לולב home with his son, his servant, or his messenger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports אמימר's practice. People in ירושלים held the לולב even while praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows the לולב was held during קריאת שמע and תפילה, which matches אמימר. It was put down only when the hands were needed, for reading the תורה or lifting the hands for ברכת כהנים. It was sent away from the בית המדרש, where Torah learning needs full attention.
steps.whatToRemember: One may hold the לולב during תפילה. A מצוה object does not distract, unlike ordinary objects. The people of ירושלים showed their love for the מצוה by carrying the לולב almost everywhere.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok says:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגָן שֶׁל אַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: This was the custom of the people of Jerusalem:
A person leaves his house — with his lulav in his hand.
He goes to the synagogue — his lulav in his hand.
He recites Shema and prays —
with his lulav in his hand.
phrases.notes: This is the direct support for אמימר.

phrases.english: When he reads the Torah or lifts his hands (for Birkas Kohanim) —
he places it on the ground.
phrases.notes: His hands are needed for these actions.

phrases.english: He goes to visit the sick and comfort mourners —
his lulav in his hand.
He enters the study hall —
he sends his lulav home with his son,
or with his servant, or with his messenger.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives support from a ברייתא for the practice defended in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The practice of holding the לולב during תפילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אלעזר בר צדוק about the custom of the people of ירושלים.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא give so many details?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what we learn from all the details in רבי אלעזר בר צדוק's description of the people of ירושלים holding their לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא lists so many examples. Every example seems to show the same thing: they held the לולב all day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes the לולב being held in shul, during קריאת שמע, during תפילה, and on visits to the sick and to mourners. If the only point were 'they held it all day,' one or two examples would be enough. So the גמרא asks what the long list adds.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? A standard question when a source seems to say something obvious or repeat itself.

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?
phrases.notes: Refers to the long list of details in the ברייתא of רבי אלעזר בר צדוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the detailed ברייתא quoted in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the purpose of the ברייתא's many details, which all seem to make the same point?

steps.title: The details show how eager they were to do מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists every detail to show how eager and careful the people were in keeping מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is to let you know how eager they were to do מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the details are not there to teach a new law. They are there to show how much the people loved מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the ברייתא is about attitude, not about a new rule. The people would not let go of the לולב even during everyday activities. This matches the theme of Step 18, which also showed how much the חכמים loved מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: Eager, quick, and careful in doing something

steps.whatToRemember: The detailed ברייתא is not about a new הלכה. It shows how eager people were to do מצוות, which the גמרא calls זריזות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the section about holding the לולב, including during תפילה. The גמרא sees eagerness to hold onto a מצוה as something worth praising.

phrases.english: To let you know how eager they were in doing מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The details teach how eager they were to do מצוות. They do not teach a separate law.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Holding the לולב all day showed the people's eagerness for מצוות.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יוסי's ruling, and אביי begins to comment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'רבי יוסי says: יום טוב' and introduces אביי, who is about to comment on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי יוסי says, 'If the first day of יום טוב [falls on שבת, and someone forgets and carries the לולב into the public domain, he is exempt].' אביי said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by going back to the משנה and quoting רבי יוסי. It then begins אביי's comment, which continues on the next עמוד. This line is setting up what comes there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי rules on a case where the first day of סוכות falls on שבת. Someone forgets it is שבת and carries his לולב into רשות הרבים. רבי יוסי says he is פטור and does not bring a חטאת, because he carried it while busy with a מצוה. אביי is about to explain exactly when this exemption applies.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא in the משנה who rules that this person is exempt
Festival day; here, the first day of סוכות falling on שבת
Exempt; here, he does not need to bring a חטאת
An אמורא who is about to limit רבי יוסי's ruling

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'יום טוב' are only a short quote of the משנה. The full case is the first day of the festival falling on שבת, when someone forgets and carries the לולב. אביי's actual statement comes on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: [If the first] day of the Festival [fell on Shabbat, one who carried the lulav is exempt].
phrases.notes: A short quote of the משנה. Its full ruling: he is פטור because he carried it while doing a מצוה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
phrases.notes: Introduces אביי's comment, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of eagerness for the לולב and returns to the next ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: if the first day of יום טוב falls on שבת and someone forgets and carries the לולב into רשות הרבים, he is exempt from a חטאת. אביי is about to comment on this.
